Subject Code 
SD5979 
Subject Title 
Research Methods for Multimedia Entertainment 
Credit Value 
3 
Level 
5 
Pre-requisite/ 
Co-requisite/Exclusion 
/ 
Objectives 
 
In this course, multimedia entertainment students will gain a 
robust proficiency in quantitative design research. They will 
acquire a comprehensive understanding of the diverse research 
methods and statistical techniques that form the backbone of 
successful scientific investigation. 
Students will learn to meticulously construct research design 
outlines that are well-informed and thoroughly planned. This 
course also aims to instil a deep understanding of data literacy, 
which is a fundamental skill in today's data-driven landscape. 
Students will not only learn to effectively gather and manage 
data, but also to interpret and analyse it in meaningful ways. 
They will be trained to identify patterns, draw insights, and 
make informed decisions based on the data at hand. This skill 
will be particularly beneficial when tackling complex problems 
or creating innovative solutions in the multimedia 
entertainment industry. 
This course equips students with the critical skills to handle 
quantitative data confidently, ensuring they are well-prepared 
for the challenges and opportunities multimedia entertainment 
research.  
Intended Learning 
Outcomes 
(Note 1) 
Upon completion of the subject, students will be able to: 
  
Professional Skills 
a. Acquire comprehensive understanding of qualitative and 
statistical techniques enabling them to effectively 
employ these methods in their scientific endeavours.  
b. Develop a solid foundation in data literacy, enabling 
them to effectively gather, manage, interpret, and 
analyse qualitative and quantitative data.  
c. Explain, identify and describe the difference between 
qualitative and quantitative research approaches and 
methods.

Subject Synopsis/ 
Indicative Syllabus 
(Note 2)  
Quantitively Research Methods 
 Observation protocols  
 Field experiments  
 Lab experiments  
 Respondent strategies  
 Theoretical strategies  
 Within-between designs  
 Solomon 4-group design 
 Confounds, experimenter bias, pseudo-randomization  
 Structured questionnaire design Dos and don’ts of 
(psycho)physiological measurement 
 
Qualitative Research Methods 
 
Overview of qualitative research methods 
 
Different types of qualitative research methods (e.g. 
ethnography, grounded theory, phenomenology, case study) 
 
Data collection methods for qualitative research (interviews, 
observations, focus groups, documentary analysis) 
Test theory  
 Frequentist testing, Bayesian classification  
 Normal distributions, mean, modus, median, standard 
deviations, rejection area, confidence intervals, effect 
sizes G-power  
 Validity and Reliability in Qualitative Research 
Research Analysis  
 Pearson product-moment correlation Cronbach’s alpha 
Principal Component Analysis Outlier analysis t-test, 
Oneway, ANOVA, MANOVA, MANCOVA General linear 
model (Univariate, Multivariate, Repeated Measures) 
(Multiple) regression, part and partial correlations 
Mediation-moderation analysis 
 Thematic Analysis, Discourse Analysis, Grounded Theory 
Analysis

Explanation of the appropriateness of the assessment methods 
in assessing the intended learning outcomes: 
 
Assignments offer students the chance to practice and 
demonstrate their understanding of research methods and 
statistical techniques, along with their ability to gather, manage, 
and interpret quantitative data. The project and exams will 
provide a more applied setting where students can employ their 
data analysis skills and make informed decisions based on the 
quantitative data at hand. Project writeups will allow students 
to showcase their ability to apply research skills in the context of 
multimedia entertainment. They will have the opportunity to 
tackle complex research questions and outline their innovative 
research design and analysis, thus showing their comprehension 
and application of the course's learning objectives.
